causal_path: Original RequestCompletion.abort_and_await sends lifecycle :abort then awaits logical cleanup (request_completion.ex99-102; whole file identical).

Lifecycle handles :abort by enumerating resources and cancelling each. Owner cancellation sends :abort (line458); socket cancellation applies linger and closes TCP port (475-477). Map traversal/send order does not force owner to consume abort before setopts. Whole lifecycle file identical.

send_request1765 returns transport.send result selected from its mailbox. Byte-identical function retains potential final-send error arriving ahead of pendingabort. Peer complete-header notification alone does not prove owner has consumed final-send result or entered response loop.

initialize_legacy_owner558-571 performs request_ready before start_prepared_request; following successful send it calls activate_socket immediately, with no new intervening cancellationcause arbitration. activate_socket1959-1967 still returns raw setopts error and closes socket; function byte-identical.
fail1567-1577 normalizes only :timeout after originaldeadline; :einval is unchanged. report_failure1582-1584 triggers cleanup then sends originalreason. Functions unchanged.

await_owner1664-1666 forwards raw http_fetch_error reason. Its only source change is timeout+1000 delegated to owner_wait_timeout, identical behavior for finite3000. Promise, RequestCompletion and AbortController unchanged; HTTP.ex difference is documentation only.

Thus cleanup can close TCP while owner is activating/final-sending, letting raw transport error win over pendingabort. The actual original failing syscall/interleaving remains untraced. No new runtime reproduction performed.

linked_repair_pr.title: fix: support infinite HTTP1 request deadlines
linked_repair_pr.body:
HTTP/1 requests using `timeout: :infinity` crashed while calculating their deadline. Preserve an unlimited request deadline and an independent finite or infinite connection timeout, including raw streaming uploads/downloads, cancellation, owner cleanup, and connection reuse.

ExSSL streaming uploads retain a finite per-write limit. Document that limit, separate stream/Promise timeouts, and the existing finite-timeout requirement for managed scopes. Add the v0.21.9 changelog entry.

Validation: strict compilation in default and test environments; full Fetch suite (20 doctests, 951 tests, zero failures); focused real TCP/OTP TLS/ExSSL regressions; root formatting; Credo (496 files, no issues). The focused tests cover stalled setup, blocked TLS uploads, raw streaming, abort/caller/reader death, and reuse.

Fixes #119
